topics.intent: Python developer wants a Browser Use agent to continue in a Chrome session that is already open, including its existing page state.
topics.unique_scope: Browser Use Python BrowserSession / BrowserProfile CDP setup, current Chrome 136+ dedicated user-data-directory requirement, endpoint check, limited sample task, and verified keep_alive / Agent.run cleanup semantics.

official_sources.title: Browser Use Python CDP example
official_sources.supports: Current repository example attaches BrowserSession via BrowserProfile(cdp_url=..., is_local=True), runs an Agent on it, and calls session.kill() after the run. The article does not copy this cleanup unmodified because Agent.run() invokes Agent.close() in its own finally path.

official_sources.title: Browser Use browser configuration reference
official_sources.supports: Documents cdp_url as the connection setting for an existing browser instance.

official_sources.title: Browser Use BrowserSession implementation
official_sources.supports: Current source says stop() requests a non-forced browser stop and the BrowserSession stop handler preserves the process when BrowserProfile.keep_alive is true; kill() sends a forced stop that bypasses keep_alive.

official_sources.title: Chrome for Developers: Changes to remote debugging switches to improve security
official_sources.supports: From Chrome 136, --remote-debugging-port and --remote-debugging-pipe are ignored for the default Chrome data directory and must be paired with a non-standard --user-data-dir.

official_sources.title: Browser Use repository quickstart
official_sources.supports: Python library quickstart and current project overview; repository currently documents Python 3.11+ for the Python library.

official_sources.title: Browser Use BrowserProfile source
official_sources.supports: Current BrowserProfile defines keep_alive with default None and describes it as keeping the browser alive after an agent run.

official_sources.title: Browser Use Agent lifecycle source
official_sources.supports: Current Agent.close() kills the browser session when browser_profile.keep_alive is false or unset. With keep_alive true, it stops the event bus without killing the browser; Agent.run() cleanup calls close().

Keep both labeled by provenance, and do not use either exact count/date as a current-hotness claim.

source_gaps: An earlier pass inferred that BrowserSession.stop() alone would preserve Chrome after agent.run(); that was incomplete. Agent.run() closes the Agent, and Agent.close() kills the session unless BrowserProfile.keep_alive is true. The template and article now set keep_alive=True explicitly. An explicit forced kill still closes the browser.
No Browser Use installation or live Chrome session was run for this assignment; the Python example is source-checked, not reported as executed.

correction_evidence.finding: Agent.run() cleanup closes Agent; Agent.close() calls BrowserSession.kill() when keep_alive is false or unset. keep_alive=True makes Agent.close() release the event bus without killing the browser. BrowserSession’s non-forced stop handler also preserves the browser when keep_alive is true; force=True still stops it.
